title: Septic arthritis of the native knee

header.contentArea: Trauma and orthopaedics: musculoskeletal infection (clinical scenario with examiner-supplied findings)
guidelineVersions: BOASt: Management of musculoskeletal soft tissue infections, including native large joint infections (July 2025)
BOASt: Acute Management of Peri-Prosthetic Joint Infection (October 2023)
BSR guideline scope: septic arthritis in adults with a hot swollen joint (Arumalla et al., 2025)

brief.role: Core surgical trainee on call for orthopaedics
brief.scenario: Mr Callum Strachan, 55, has type 2 diabetes. His GP injected steroid into his right knee for osteoarthritis five days ago. For two days the knee has been hot, swollen and too painful to bear weight. Temperature 38.3°C.
brief.task: Answer the examiner's questions on his assessment and immediate management.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Septic arthritis until proven otherwise. Is he septic? That decides antibiotics or aspiration first.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Starting antibiotics in a stable patient before the joint is aspirated.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "This is septic arthritis until proven otherwise. First I'd check whether he has sepsis."

grid.label: Working diagnosis and differentials
grid.fail: Calls it a post-injection flare or gout and plans discharge.
grid.pass: Septic arthritis until proven otherwise. Differentials: gout, calcium pyrophosphate disease, post-injection flare, haemarthrosis, reactive or inflammatory arthritis.
grid.high: Adds that normal inflammatory markers do not exclude septic arthritis; the aspirate decides.

grid.label: History and risk factors
grid.fail: Does not ask about the injection or his diabetes.
grid.pass: Recent joint injection, diabetes, rheumatoid arthritis, prosthetic joint, previous surgery, immunosuppression, skin infection.
grid.high: Looks for another source and a cardiovascular examination for endocarditis; asks about recent antibiotics, which reduce culture yield.

grid.label: Assesses for sepsis
grid.fail: Does not check observations or lactate before deciding.
grid.pass: Full observations and lactate; if septic, Sepsis Six now and inform the on-call orthopaedic team.
grid.high: States the sepsis decision changes the order: septic patients get antibiotics after blood cultures, without waiting for aspiration.

grid.label: Aspirates before antibiotics when stable
grid.fail: Gives antibiotics first 'to be safe' in a stable patient.
grid.pass: Not septic: no antibiotics until aspirated. Aseptic aspiration, avoiding cellulitic skin; Gram stain, culture, cell count and crystals. Blood cultures.
grid.high: Would use ultrasound guidance if the aspirate is dry, and records the colour and turbidity of the fluid.

grid.label: Antibiotics
grid.fail: Gives oral antibiotics, or delays them after sampling.
grid.pass: Once samples are taken, IV antibiotics per local microbiology policy, covering staphylococci and streptococci; adjust to culture.
grid.high: Covers MRSA if he is colonised or at risk; notes a prolonged course, initially IV, guided by microbiology.

grid.label: Washout
grid.fail: Treats with antibiotics alone and no orthopaedic plan.
grid.pass: Urgent orthopaedic washout, arthroscopic or open. If septic and acutely unwell, surgery within 6 hours unless there is a specific reason not to.
grid.high: Explains cartilage damage is time-critical; repeat washout if local or systemic signs persist.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Any other infection source, a cardiovascular examination for endocarditis, and whether he's had antibiotics recently, because that lowers the culture yield.

high.text: Why does sepsis matter for the order of things?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: If he's septic, blood cultures then antibiotics straight away; I wouldn't wait for aspiration. If he's stable, I aspirate first.

high.text: Ultrasound-guided aspiration, or sampling in theatre. I'd record the colour and turbidity whenever fluid comes.

failures.move: Starting antibiotics before aspirating a stable patient's joint.
failures.consequence: Cultures may be sterile, so the organism and the right antibiotic are never identified.

failures.move: Delaying antibiotics in a septic patient to aspirate first.
failures.consequence: Sepsis progresses; septic patients need cultures and antibiotics immediately.

failures.move: Labelling it a post-injection flare and discharging him.
failures.consequence: Untreated infection destroys cartilage and can cause sepsis.
Pus stays in the joint and cartilage loss continues.

recovery.line: It depends on sepsis: septic, cultures and antibiotics now; stable, aspirate first.
Normal markers don't exclude septic arthritis; the aspirate decides.

knowledge.fact: Native joint infections follow the peri-prosthetic joint infection BOASt standards; the aspirate includes crystals.
Septic: Sepsis Six, blood cultures, then antibiotics; surgery within 6 hours if acutely unwell.
Not septic: no antibiotics until deep samples are taken.
Risk factors: joint injection or surgery, rheumatoid arthritis, prosthesis, skin infection, diabetes, immunosuppression.
Normal inflammatory markers do not exclude septic arthritis.

recall.think: Sepsis, and cartilage destroyed within days.
recall.say: "Septic arthritis until proven otherwise. Is he septic?"

numbers.meaning: surgery if septic and acutely unwell

recall.trap: A normal CRP does not exclude septic arthritis.
recall.finish: Arthroscopic or open washout, repeated if needed; microbiology-guided antibiotics.

sources.name: BOASt: Management of musculoskeletal soft tissue infections: life-threatening conditions including necrotising fasciitis and myositis; native large joint infections; abscesses and cellulitis (British Orthopaedic Association)
sources.supports: Sepsis Six immediately for sepsis; native joint infections treated to the peri-prosthetic joint infection BOASt standards, recognising the time-critical nature of chondral injury; aspirate to include samples for crystallography

sources.name: BOASt: Acute Management of Peri-Prosthetic Joint Infection (British Orthopaedic Association)
sources.supports: Sepsis Six and inform on-call orthopaedics; blood cultures then parenteral antibiotics; surgery within 6 hours in an acutely unwell patient unless specific reasons; no antibiotics in a non-septic patient until deep samples taken; assess for other infection sources and endocarditis; record recent antibiotics

sources.name: Arumalla N, Allen VB, Shah K, et al. Management of septic arthritis in adults with a hot swollen joint: British Society for Rheumatology guideline scope. Rheumatol Adv Pract 2025;9(3):rkaf058
sources.supports: Risk factors (previous joint surgery, RA, prosthetic joints, recent joint injection, skin infection, diabetes, immunosuppression); differentials of a hot swollen joint; normal inflammatory markers do not exclude septic arthritis; empirical broad-spectrum antibiotics covering staphylococci and streptococci, varied for MRSA risk and directed by local microbiology; prolonged course, initially IV; washout often needed and repeated if treatment fails

sources.name: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery (O'Connell, McCaskie, Sayers, eds)
sources.supports: Septic arthritis: differentials of the acute hot swollen joint; risk factors; assessment for another source including endocarditis; joint aspiration before antibiotics; empirical IV antibiotics covering staphylococci and streptococci, including MRSA when at risk, adjusted to culture, with a prolonged course

partner.opening: Mr Strachan's knee is hot and swollen. What is your working diagnosis?

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks for observations and lactate
reveals.finding: Heart rate 96, BP 136/84, RR 18, SpO2 97% on air, alert. Lactate 1.2 mmol/L.
Large effusion, warm, painful on any movement; no overlying cellulitis; the injection site has healed.
Turbid yellow fluid. Gram stain awaited.

push.question: What is the working diagnosis?
push.expect: Septic arthritis until proven otherwise; list differentials.

push.question: What decides whether you aspirate or give antibiotics first?
push.expect: Sepsis. Septic: cultures and antibiotics now. Stable: aspirate first.

push.question: What do you send the aspirate for?
push.expect: Gram stain, culture, cell count, crystals.

push.question: Which antibiotic?
push.expect: IV, local policy, covering staphylococci and streptococci.

push.question: Does he need surgery?
push.expect: Urgent washout; within 6 hours if septic and acutely unwell.

curveballs.prompt: While you wait for the aspiration kit, his BP falls to 88/50, HR 124, and he is confused.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Now septic: Sepsis Six, blood cultures and IV antibiotics immediately; don't wait to aspirate; emergency washout within 6 hours; senior help.

curveballs.prompt: The aspirate shows negatively birefringent needle-shaped crystals.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Gout, but await Gram stain and culture before excluding infection given his risk factors.

curveballs.prompt: The knee is a total knee replacement.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Peri-prosthetic joint infection: follow the PJI BOASt. Don't aspirate in ED; urgent orthopaedic review; aspiration by the orthopaedic team under strict asepsis; no antibiotics until deep samples unless septic; assess for endocarditis.
